header.title: The Sensory World of Atelier Verdant

body_sections.heading: Opening
body_sections.prose: Atelier Verdant sounds like footsteps on bleached oak. It smells of starched linen and beeswax. It tastes of well-water and a slice of pear. It looks like late afternoon, not noon. It feels like a heavy door closing softly behind you.

body_sections.heading: The Five Senses
body_sections.prose: The sensory map is a working brief, not a mood board. Every sense has a position the brand defends in the field of competitors who default to gloss, speed, and noise.

body_sections.heading: Sensory Anti-Patterns
body_sections.prose: The brand is not bright. Not glossy. Not loud. Not floral. Not synthetic. Not warm-LED. Anti-patterns are non-negotiable: they're the surface where the brand can be most easily diluted by a freelancer or a vendor on a deadline.

body_sections.heading: Sensory Decisions Ahead
body_sections.prose: Three decisions are imminent: the studio's daylight palette under cloud cover, the smell of the showroom and what fills its air, the speech tempo of the founder's voice in product video.
